title: What our drives have taught us · AquaTerra
description: What AquaTerra's drives teach about small crews, repeatable formats, named skills and counting attendance, across {count} drives in Kolkata.
lede: Every AquaTerra drive is written up, and read together they show what works. Small crews carry most of the work, simple formats travel from place to place, and drives that name the skill they teach are the easiest to learn from. Since {firstYear}, that adds up to {count} drives and {volunteers} volunteer turnouts.

sections.heading: small crews do most of the work
body: Most drives run with a small crew of a few people, and some run with one or two. The largest turnouts come from events rather than everyday work. The Disco Diwali fundraiser at 60 Chowrangee Banquet and the Starry Night fundraiser at Sky Turf are the biggest entries, well ahead of the feeding and teaching drives. Festival drives are a group of their own, with {count:festival-drives} drives so far.

The turnout figures point to two sizes of work: small crews for everyday drives, and larger groups for events. That matters when a team plans its next drive, because a crew of a few people can run a feeding or card drive on its own.

sections.heading: a simple format travels
body: The Smile Notes campaign shows how a format travels. The same idea, a written note of encouragement handed out with a toffee, has appeared at Bhawanipore, MBA Chaiwala Lake Town, Lake Town Footbridge and Bangur between March and May 2026. The Cookie Pass On drives in December 2025 work the same way: volunteers gave cookies to residents at Barrackpore, Silver Spring Apartment, Astitva Apartment and Avani Oxford, and asked each resident to pass one on.

sections.heading: naming the skill makes a drive easier to judge
body: The April 2026 teaching drives name what was taught. The Build-a-Sentence Lab at Disha Foundation and the Sentence Secrets session at Ek Tara both covered subjects and predicates with worksheets, and the Teaching English Workshop at Ektara Foundation covered conjunctions and verbs. A reader can see exactly what the children were taught.

Compare that with Art Alley, which describes itself as sparking creativity and expression, and says how many children were taught. The first kind of drive is easier to learn from, because you can judge whether the lesson went where it was meant to.

sections.heading: what gets counted
body: Most key figures count what was handed out or who turned up: notes and toffees, dogs fed, kilograms of clothes, books collected, children taught and cookies given out. Few say what a child could do afterwards. The exceptions are the teaching drives that name the skill, and the Digital Safety Workshop at Pather Sathi, which says children were given digital safety knowledge without describing a test or a follow-up.

A stronger account would say what changed for the children, not only how many came, and would give a turnout for every drive, including the Learner's Den session that has none. That is a suggestion for future drive pages, not a claim about results that have been measured.

sections.heading: the series that last are the simple ones
body: The drives that keep coming back are the ones a small group can run without much setup. Grow Green, the plantation series, has run {count:grow-green} drives since 2021. Tails and Treats, the stray dog feeding series, has run {count:tails-and-treats} since 2022. Sharbat Seva has come back every summer since 2024 with {count:sharbat-seva} drives. Each one needs a place, a few people and one simple thing to hand out or plant.

That is also why a new member can start quickly. Joining a series that already runs means learning one format from people who have done it before, then running it in a new neighbourhood. The [how a drive works](/impact/how-a-drive-works) page walks through it, and [volunteering for teenagers in Kolkata](/impact/volunteering-for-teens-in-kolkata) covers how to join.

learnings: Everyday drives run with small crews, and the largest turnouts come from events.
A simple format such as Smile Notes or the Cookie Pass On can be repeated across many places.
Naming the skill taught, as the April 2026 English sessions did, makes a drive easier to judge.
Most drives count attendance and output, so they show reach more than learning.
Series that need only a place, a few people and one simple thing to hand out are the ones that keep running.

faqs.q: What has AquaTerra learned from its drives?
faqs.a: The drives suggest that small crews can repeat a simple format across many places, that naming the skill taught makes a drive easier to judge, and that counts of attendance do not show learning on their own. AquaTerra has run {count} drives since {firstYear}.

faqs.q: What kind of drive does AquaTerra run most?
faqs.a: Arts and crafts is the largest theme, with {count:arts-and-crafts} drives so far, and animal welfare follows with {count:animal-welfare}. Feeding stray dogs is the largest named series, with {count:tails-and-treats} Tails and Treats drives.

Yes. AquaTerra runs clothes collections. Its Wear and Share drives collected clothes in neighbourhoods in July 2025, and a Clothes Segregation and Donation drive took clothes to Goonj in Kolkata in September 2025. There is no standing drop-off point in the drive pages, so check with the team through the [contact page](/contact) before you bring clothes.

faqs.q: Does AquaTerra publish what it does?
faqs.a: Yes. Each drive is listed with its date, place, objective, volunteer turnout and usually a key figure. AquaTerra has run {count} drives since {firstYear}, and {year:2026} of them fall in 2026 so far.
